text:
I have a question for couples where one partner went through an Orthodox conversion with the Rabbanut, and whether you felt it was necessary to do a second Orthodox conversion afterward.

For context, I recently completed my Orthodox conversion through the Rabbanut in Israel, but I’ve been told that it may not be recognized by certain communities/authorities in the UK and the Netherlands. I understand there is an option to undergo another conversion through a Haredi Beit Din in Bnei Brak that may have broader recognition.

I don’t currently plan on living in either of those countries, so this doesn’t directly affect me right now. My main concern is my future children. I want to give them the best opportunities possible and avoid them ever having to deal with questions about their Jewish status.

The whole situation has become really stressful. Conversion isn’t an easy process, and I don’t want to put myself through another one unnecessarily, but I also don’t want my children to face this issue someday.

I’d really appreciate hearing from anyone who has been in a similar situation or has experience with recognition of Rabbanut conversions.
